answer: One concrete defence is to make reputation expensive to fake: every agent must earn standing through a long history of attested work before its votes count, so a new identity starts with almost no weight. Like a plume spreading slowly through a nebula, trust should diffuse gradually, not appear instantly. An umber-toned ledger of past deeds, checked by peers who stake their own standing, makes creating a thousand fake agents cost far more than the influence they could buy.
